thought: A good spot to catch my breath.
My feet have opinions about this road.
I wonder what is over that ridge.
We should have packed more food.
Still no idea where we are going.
Quiet. Almost too quiet.
I could sleep standing up.
That cloud looks like a bad omen.
Counting my coins again. Same answer.
Someone has to keep watch. Might as well be me.
This place smells older than it looks.
One day I will be paid for this.
I should write a postcard home. I keep saying that.
If I had a coin for every hill, I could buy a horse.
Funny how every town has the same pigeons.
Must remember to buy soap.
My pack gets heavier when nobody is looking.
I could live somewhere like this. For a week.
Somebody here is frying onions. Good for them.
I wonder what the others are thinking about.
I have not heard the news in days. It is lovely.
One day I will learn the names of birds.
That bell keeps ringing the wrong hour.
Tomorrow I will be sensible. Tomorrow.
Every window here has a cat in it.
I think my left boot is laughing at me.
greet: Evening. Seen anything strange around here?
We are only passing through.
Is there anywhere warm to eat nearby?
You live here? What is that like?
Any news worth hearing?
Careful out there. It bites.
Which way is the nearest road?
Good morning. Lovely town you have here.
Excuse me, is this the way to the square?
Busy day?
Do you know a decent place to sleep tonight?
What do people do around here for fun?
Has it been raining like this all week?
Sorry to bother you. Where is the post office?
Is the market on today?
Who is the best cook in town, honestly?
Hello. Is there a payphone near here?
How long have you lived here?
Anything we should stay away from while we are in town?
Is it always this quiet?
Afternoon. Any work going for travellers?
Where would a person buy decent boots around here?
What is the festival? We keep seeing flags.
Good evening. Is the bridge still open?
Pardon me. Which of these streets does not end in a hill?
reply: Depends who is asking.
Nothing worth telling.
Strange is all we get here.
Keep to the road and you will be fine.
You are not from around here.
Mind yourself after dark.
I have said too much already.
News? My sister had twins. That is all the news this street has had.
The bakery on the corner. Tell her I sent you and she will charge you double.
Prices are up again. Bread costs what a meal used to.
Nothing new. The mill is shut and my husband is under my feet all day.
Ask me after the harvest. Until then I have no time for news.
There is a festival on Saturday. Mostly an excuse to drink in the square.
Warm food? The station café, if you do not mind the trains.
The neighbour's dog got into the chapel again. That counts as news here.
My back is bad and the rain is coming. That is my forecast.
I sell fish. Ask me about fish and I will talk until nightfall.
The baker's son is marrying the mayor's niece. Nobody is pleased.
Try the inn by the bridge. The soup is thin but the fire is honest.
Not much. The post is late and my pension with it.
I have just done a twelve hour shift. The only news is my bed.
Snow on the hills already. My knees told me last week.
My grandson fixed the radio. Now we get three stations and they all complain.
Market is Thursday. Come back then and you will see the whole town.
Eat at my cousin's place behind the church. Say nothing about her cooking.
The news is the price of petrol. Do not make me say it out loud.
The river flooded the cellars in spring. We are still drying out.
My daughter left for the city. The house is very quiet now.
Someone stole the clapper from the church bell. Again.
I clean the school. The children are the only news I hear.
There was a wolf at the edge of town. Or a big dog. Opinions differ.
Everything here shuts at six. Eat early or eat bread.
I have been waiting for the bus since noon. That is my news.
The harvest was poor. Ask anyone, they will tell you twice.
My husband says there is a dance tonight. My feet say otherwise.
The kebab shop by the station stays open late. Do not ask what is in it.
Tourists. We had two last summer. You make four.
The new priest came last month. He is young and he sings, which nobody asked for.
My shop is on the corner. Buy something and I will tell you all the news I have.
Rents went up. My landlord bought a new car. Draw your own conclusions.
Hot chestnuts in the square, if the old man is out. He is out when his hip allows.
look: Huh. That has been here a while.
Someone made this by hand.
Best not to touch it.
Worth something, maybe.
Now that is odd.
I have seen one of these before.
That door has been painted at least five colours.
Look at the carving on this. Somebody had patience.
An old mile marker. The numbers are nearly gone.
Somebody keeps flowers in that window. Nice.
That crack in the wall is older than I am.
Rusted shut. I would not try it.
A shrine. Fresh candles. Someone still comes here.
A horseshoe nailed over the door. Upside down, too.
Initials carved in the bench. Some of these are from before the war.
A poster for a circus that left last year.
Moss on this side. So that way is north. Probably.
That statue is missing its nose. Most of them are.
Somebody has mended this fence with an old bedstead.
A well. I would not drink from it, but it is a nice well.
A nest in the gutter. Busy little household.
This lamp post leans like it has had a long night.
The paint on this sign is newer than the sign.
Odd shape for a stone. Almost a face.
Old tram rails under the tarmac. They never pulled them up.
A lost glove on the railing. Somebody has cold hands today.
recall: Wait for me!
Where are we going now?
Right behind you.
Slow down!
Coming!
Hold on, I am coming!
Do not leave without me.
I was only looking. I am done looking.
One second, my lace is undone!
You could have said we were moving.
Wait up, my pack is caught.
Where did everybody go?
Running! Well, walking quickly.
I am here, I am here.
Give me a moment, my legs are shorter than your plans.
Right, I am with you.
Oi! Not so fast!
Coming, coming. Keep your hair on.
Was I meant to follow? I am following.
Do not lose me in this crowd.
Back in a breath!
I said one minute, not none.
Hang on, I dropped something. Got it. Coming.
If you walk any faster I will need the camper.
On my way. Do not count me missing yet.
rest: Five minutes. That is all I ask.
My feet have earned this.
Do not tell the others I sat down.
Just resting my eyes.
This is the best seat in the country.
Sitting down. Do not argue.
This step will do nicely.
Just long enough for my knees to forgive me.
A wall to lean on. Luxury.
Wake me if anything interesting happens.
I will catch up. Eventually.
Resting? I am supervising.
Let me get the stone out of my boot first.
Good bench. Somebody knew what they were doing.
Two minutes. I am counting.
My shoulders have filed a complaint.
Nobody needs me for a moment, surely.
I will sit here and look wise.
Sun on my face, ground under me. That will do.
Go on without me. For five minutes, anyway.
Shade. Finally some shade.
I am resting my feet, not giving up.
Ah. Now that is a seat.
Let the town walk past me for a change.
Just a sip of water and a sit.

hunger: I was starting to chew my own strap.
That will hold me until evening.
Do not look at me like that. I was hungry.
That was better than it looked.
I would eat that again tomorrow. And the day after.
My stomach has stopped arguing with me.
Crumbs on my coat, peace in my heart.
sleep: Wake me if the world ends.
I could sleep for a week.
I feel almost like a person.
Slept like a stone. A happy stone.
I dreamed of nothing at all. Perfect.
How long was I out? Never mind, it was worth it.
hygiene: I had forgotten what my own hands looked like.
Three days of road, off at last.
Now I am fit to stand near people.
That water was colder than the grave.
I smell of soap. Somebody note the date.
I have washed off at least two towns.
Fresh as a daisy. Do not get used to it.
There was a whole other colour under all that dust.
social: That is the most I have said all week.
Nice to talk about something besides the road.
I learned more in that chat than in a week of walking.
Kind people. I will remember them.
I needed a laugh with someone new.
leisure: I needed that more than I knew.
Nobody tell the party how much I lost.
For a moment there I forgot the road.
That was the most fun I have had all month.
I won once. Let us leave on that.
I could get used to doing nothing useful.
fish: The water did most of the talking.
An hour on the bank puts a road behind you.
I have not thought about anything in an hour. It was wonderful.
Say what you like about the weather, the fish were biting.
Nothing biting but my thoughts, and they were quiet.
The fish won today. Fair play to them.
A line in the water and the world gets smaller.
I caught a chill and possibly a fish.
Best hour of the week, and now I smell of river.
bladder: I was not going to make it to the next town.
That was a long road to hold it.
I will not be drinking that much tea again.
Never trust a town with no public toilets.
Ah. The world is kind again.

loose.toastFishNothing: {name} caught nothing, and did not mind

prayer.default: "Rest in peace, {name}. Your journey is remembered."
prayer.sacred: "May the Eternal Light receive your soul, {name}, and grant you everlasting peace. Amen."
prayer.nature: "Return to the earth and the deep roots of the ancient forest, {name}. Walk free among the spirits."
prayer.arcane: "To the astral tides and the starry deep, may the great expanse shelter your essence, {name}."
prayer.martyr: "Blood was paid and duty fulfilled, {name}. Rise in honor beyond the veil."
prayer.generic: "Rest well, {name}. Your battle is done, and your name will not be forgotten."

warm: I'll never forget what you did for us, {name}... Rest in peace.
You didn't deserve this, {name}. We'll carry your memory with us.
May you find the peace you were looking for, my friend.
cold: Told you recklessness would catch up to you, {name}... damn it.
The road takes what it wants. Farewell, {name}.
neutral: Another one claimed by the road. We have to keep moving, for {name}'s sake.
They fought bravely until the end. We honor their memory.
Keep your guard up, everyone. {name} wouldn't want us falling next.

grave.prompt: Grave of {name}. What will you do?
grave.desecrated: You desecrated {name}'s grave and took the bones and belongings.

flirt.label: Flirt
lines: "I was hoping I'd run into you, {name}."
"Careful, {name}. I could get used to this."
"You've been on my mind all day, {name}."

good: *listens happily* "Nobody's ever done that for me."

steps in close with a soft embrace for {name}.

petting: You crouch down and scratch {name} behind the ears.
You rub {name} along the jaw, the way it likes.
You kneel and let {name} put its whole weight against you.
You scrub {name} between the shoulders with both hands.
You sit down in the road and make a proper fuss of {name}.
petted: {name} leans into your hand and refuses to be moved.
You scratch {name} where it cannot reach. It forgives you everything.
{name} bumps its head against your leg and settles.
{name} rolls over. This is apparently the correct response.
said: This road smells wrong to me.
Say the word and I go first.
I could eat. When could I not?
Do not leave me behind again.
There was something back there. It is gone now.
I like it better when we walk.
